answer: Because the karst liability is recorded in the pulse ledger at admission, the thread audit makes public the shared exposure and internal sponsorship is self-defeating. A farm must as a result place its own capital behind each extra identity it sponsors, which is the same as paying the bond twice for each key it runs. A sponsor carries 41% of any slash its member incurs, so vouching is a financial position rather than a courtesy. That is 25 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
